kpi_specs.name: Total Revenue
kpi_specs.description: The sum of all invoice totals to measure overall sales performance.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT SUM(Total) AS total_revenue FROM data
kpi_specs.reasoning: Total revenue is the primary financial metric and is best represented as a single big number (card) for executive dashboards.

kpi_specs.name: Average Invoice Value
kpi_specs.description: The average value of transactions, helping to understand basket size and customer purchasing power.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT AVG(Total) AS avg_invoice_value FROM data
kpi_specs.reasoning: Average transaction value is a key efficiency metric in retail, best displayed on a single-value card.

kpi_specs.name: Revenue by Country
kpi_specs.description: Total sales volume aggregated by billing country to identify primary geographic markets.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT BillingCountry, SUM(Total) AS revenue FROM data GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY revenue DESC
kpi_specs.reasoning: A bar chart is ideal for comparing a numerical measure (revenue) across a categorical dimension (BillingCountry) with moderate cardinality.

kpi_specs.name: Monthly Revenue Trend
kpi_specs.description: The historical trend of monthly sales to evaluate growth patterns and seasonality.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', InvoiceDate) AS month, SUM(Total) AS monthly_revenue FROM data GROUP BY month ORDER BY month ASC
kpi_specs.reasoning: A line chart is the standard visual representation for showing continuous trends and performance patterns over chronological intervals.

kpi_specs.name: Top Customers by Total Spend
kpi_specs.description: A ranking of the top 10 customers based on their cumulative purchase totals to identify high-value clients.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT CustomerId, COUNT(InvoiceId) AS transaction_count, SUM(Total) AS total_spent FROM data GROUP BY CustomerId ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 10
kpi_specs.reasoning: A table is appropriate here as it allows business analysts to view multiple attributes (ID, transaction frequency, and total spend) for the highest-value segment.
